title: The product's own in-page card feed shape, as a two-card array, mistypes clickurl

source.name: ortbtools knowledge base — in-page native widget card
source.notes: Field shape is the product's own documented in-page widget card sample, reproduced as a two-element array (the KB file itself ships a one-element array) to exercise the array/multi-material form.

modifications: Card ids, titles, image/click/impression URLs and advertiser domain independently authored per card; the KB sample's cdn.example/click.example/imp.example hosts replaced with this corpus's assets/advertiser/tracking.example.test convention.
A second synthetic card was added; the KB sample ships only one.
provenance.sanitized: No real advertiser or subscriber data; all hosts are reserved .test domains; price values are small synthetic placeholders.

specNotes: packages/core/detect.js routes every JSON array unconditionally to TYPES.VENDOR_FEED (no shape check at the type-detection layer); packages/core/rules-feed.js then routes every array unconditionally to validatePushMaterialsFeed(), which checks the click role via click_url|link only — this card's clickurl (no separator) satisfies neither alias, so feed.push.click_url_required (ERROR) fires per element even though price/title/image/icon are all recognised by their own alias pairs.

packages/core/format-detect.js detectFeedFormat() iterates every array element independently and unions the tags; its hasClick set includes clickurl, so FORMATS.INPAGE is still tagged correctly for the whole array despite the per-element validation false positive — the same disagreement as the single-object sibling case, now doubled (one false error per card).
DEF-201 closed 2026-09-08: the Inspector now offers a bid/material selector whenever a response carries more than one candidate, so this case's second card is reachable through the UI like the first.
notes: No request side exists for this scenario, for the same reason as the single-object sibling case.

DEF-181 (clickurl alias, packages/core + this file's Inspector) and DEF-201 (bid/material selector) are both closed as of 2026-09-08; this case carries no knownGap and is expected to pass normatively.
